tools.name: agent_teams_control
tools.description: Halt or resume the team. `halt` stops NEW DISPATCH and leaves the team and every teammate alive (use agent_teams_plan action:"delete" to end a team). `resume` clears the hold.

reason.description: halt: why the team is halted; shown to anyone who asks for status.

tools.name: agent_teams_dispatch
tools.description: Pair READY shared tasks with IDLE members. `run` pairs each ready task with one idle member and RECORDS the pairing (no second pass can hand it to another member; the ledger is TEAM-SCOPED, so two teams in one workspace never shadow each other). Unpaired tasks are reported with their reason. `release` frees a pairing and reopens the task row to `pending`.

tools.name: agent_teams_mail
tools.description: The team mailbox. `send` messages one member (through the official transport) and records it; `unread` lists what a member has NOT acknowledged; `read` acknowledges ids; `summary` counts total/unread/undelivered per member. Delivery and reading are separate facts: a message the transport accepted is still unread until the recipient acknowledges it.

to.description: send: the member name or id to message.

subject.description: send: one line the recipient sees first.

member.description: unread: whose inbox (defaults to the caller).

ids.description: read: the message ids to acknowledge.

tools.name: agent_teams_plan
tools.description: The team PLAN. `create` stages (spawns nothing); `add_member`/`create_task` append to it or the live team; `edit` reads or replaces it; `approve` EXECUTES through the TEAM EXECUTOR (native default, official fallback), REFUSING an EMPTY plan; `delete` archives; `status` shows plan, hold, roster and board.

description.description: create/edit: what the team is for.

replace.description: create: to replace an ALREADY APPROVED plan.

member.description: add_member: {name, prompt, description?, role?}; prompt is the instantiation prompt.

task.description: create_task: {subject, description, blocked_by, write_scopes?, owner?, kind?, coverageOf?, sourceTaskId?}; blocked_by or independent:true required.

dry_run.description: approve: report what would be created; write nothing.

tools.name: agent_teams_task
tools.description: Shared board tasks: `claim` (freezes the contract), `contract`, `release`, terminal `complete`/`fail` (owner-only; optional `note`/`expected_revision`; a FAIL unblocks dependents), `depend` (append `blocked_by`; owner or lead).

note.description: complete/fail: one line on the row.

expected_revision.description: the revision you decided on; stale refused.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: cellwork_activate
tools.description: CAPTAIN only: materialise an ACCEPTED split on the LIVE team record. Requires an accepted split of the CURRENT requirements revision (a stale split is refused unless its revision is passed explicitly). Writes one frozen contract per NEW code task, raises each owner role as a member (persona TEXT in the prompt), appends each NEW task with reviews blocked by their work task, opens a verify loop for EVERY code task that has none yet BEFORE dispatch (a kept task whose frozen contract already names a loop is left untouched), then dispatches owner-only. A failed pass is checkpointed and the SAME accepted revision resumes it; a newer accepted revision supersedes an older in-flight one (revisions never move backwards). A NEWER revision APPENDS to the same team: kept work reuses its board row, added work is appended, dropped work is marked `cancelled` and never deleted. It never re-creates the team.

revision.description: The accepted split revision to activate when the requirements moved on (explicitly acknowledges staleness).

tools.name: cellwork_context
tools.description: Any cell seat: the caller's OWN live context occupancy — used tokens, the observed window and its provenance, the ratio, the checkpoint threshold in force, and whether a checkpoint would fire at this step. Read-only; never guesses a window (provenance `no-window`/`unavailable` answers null).

tools.name: cellwork_dispatch
tools.description: CAPTAIN only: one owner-only dispatch pass over the live board. A ready task is paired ONLY with its declared owner; a busy, absent or failed owner is REPORTED and the task left pending — never substituted. Delivery goes through the team executor and is journaled.

tools.name: cellwork_handoff
tools.description: A MEMBER's checkpoint duty: validate a handoff document (task, state, decisions, artifacts, verified facts, open questions, next step), write `handoff/<member>-<n>.md`, mark the member handoff-ready and journal it. The result tells the agent to END ITS TURN; the plugin then compacts and promotes (or reseeds) it.

content.description: The complete handoff document (markdown headings or `Key:` lines).

tools.name: cellwork_inbox
tools.description: Any cell seat: read and ACKNOWLEDGE the unread cell mail addressed to this seat (its member name, or `captain`). The rows are durable; reading them appends `read` records, so a second call does not return them again.

tools.name: cellwork_recon
tools.description: PLANNER/SUBCAPTAIN only: raise ONE read-only consult (label exactly `Explorer` or `Researcher`) through the adapter's direct one-shot start path, with an explicit absolute maxDepth so the consult is a leaf. The report is returned and journaled in the cell. A composition without the child-persona seam degrades to prose read-only and says so (`personaInjected:false`).

role.description: The read-only roster role; the label is applied verbatim so the child-persona seam applies the deny list.

task.description: The one question the consult must answer.

tools.name: cellwork_requirements
tools.description: The PLANNER's tool (cell-planner only): `finalize` the agreed requirements document or `update` it. Validates the six required sections (goal, non-goals, users/consumers, constraints, acceptance criteria, open questions). `finalize` refuses an incomplete document and completes the requirements task; `update` bumps the revision and marks the current split STALE.

action.description: finalize the agreed document, or update it (bumps the revision, marks the split stale).

content.description: The full markdown document. Omit to validate the file already at <cell>/requirements.md.

tools.name: cellwork_send
tools.description: Any cell seat: send one durable cell message to `captain`, a member of this cell by name, or `<cellId>/<captain|member>` for a cell in this cell's tree (a sub-cell it registered, or its parent). The row is appended to the RECIPIENT cell's own mail log FIRST (durable), then a wake-up is attempted through the team executor when the sender is this cell's captain and the recipient holds a handle; a failed wake-up is journaled and surfaced on `cellwork_supervise`. The journal carries the `cell:<cellId>` stamp.

to.description: `captain`, a cell member's board name, or `<cellId>/<captain|member>` for a cross-cell recipient in this cell's tree.

tools.name: cellwork_split
tools.description: The SPLITTER's tool (cell-splitter only) for `submit`; any cell seat may `show` the last verdict. `submit` MEASURES every task (declared input bytes → tokens, the model-read context window) and validates the graph (dependency answer, acyclicity, write-scope ordering, verifier ≠ writer, role existence), accepting or refusing with a per-task breakdown; a refused split may be resubmitted.

action.description: submit a graph, or show the last measured verdict.

revision.description: submit: the requirements revision the graph targets; defaults to the accepted one.

key.description: Stable task key; also the contract file name.

ownerRole.description: A roster role name or a cell role.

blockedBy.description: Task keys that must close first; [] is an explicit root.

verify.description: true when this task's work needs exactly one review task.

tools.name: cellwork_start
tools.description: Open the REQUIREMENTS phase of the ACTIVE cell (captain only): validates the cell and the caller, stamps `startedAt`, writes the journal entry and reports the live team. A cell is created by `/cellwork` ALONE — this tool never starts the mode and never creates a cell. Idempotent: a second call reports the first one's result.

tools.name: cellwork_status
tools.description: Report one cell: phase, objective, captain, requirements/split revisions, members and their modes, injected checkpoints, the live team's member/task counts and the on-disk paths. Defaults to the workspace's ACTIVE cell; pass `cellId` to read another. Never mutates anything.

cellId.description: The cell to report; omitted reads the workspace's active cell.

tools.name: cellwork_stop
tools.description: End the mode (captain only): ARCHIVES the cell (no deletion), clears the guard and gives every tool back. REFUSES while a cell task is claimed or in_progress unless `force:true`, and a forced stop is journaled as such.

force.description: Stop even with live tasks; the exception is recorded in the journal.

reason.description: One line answering why the cell ends.

cellId.description: The cell to stop; omitted uses the workspace's active cell.

tools.name: cellwork_subteam
tools.description: A promoted SUBCAPTAIN's tool: register a sub-cell (parentCellId, depth+1) and receive the sub-captain directive. REFUSES `depth + 1 > cellwork.depth.max` with the exact bound. The sub-team itself is staged by the promoted agent with `agent_teams_plan`.

objective.description: The sub-cell's objective, in the user's terms.

tools.name: cellwork_supervise
tools.description: CAPTAIN only: one READ-ONLY sweep of the cell — every member's mode / handoff state / live context ratio, the pending board tasks, the stale-split flags and the unread mail (including rows whose wake-up never went out). Call it on every wake-up; it mutates nothing.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt one teammate's current turn while preserving its pending inbox. Team Lead only.

target.description: Teammate target returned by spawn_teammate or list_agents.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List the Lead and every durable teammate with an addressable target and current availability. inactive means no turn is executing, not a task result. provisioning and failed describe member creation.

tools.name: list_mcp_resource_templates
tools.description: List parameterized resource URI templates from an MCP server.

cursor.description: Continuation cursor returned by this server.

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.description: List resources available from an MCP server.

cursor.description: Continuation cursor returned by this server.

tools.name: mcp__ast_grep__rewrite
tools.description: Preview an AST-aware rewrite, or apply it. The pattern obeys the same metavariable rules as `search`; the replacement may reference only metavariables the pattern captured, and an EMPTY replacement deletes the match. Nothing is written unless `apply` is true, and a truncated preview is refused rather than applied — narrow `paths` or raise `maxMatches`, then retry. Applying is two passes (a JSON preview, then a separate `--update-all` run), so the reported counts describe the preview, and a second apply is not guaranteed to be a no-op.

pattern.description: ast-grep pattern — code, not regex. Max 16 KiB (16384 BYTES, UTF-8) — the limit counts bytes, not characters.

rewrite.description: Replacement code; empty deletes the match. Max 64 KiB (65536 BYTES, UTF-8) — the limit counts bytes, not characters.

language.description: Language the pattern must parse in.

paths.description: Files or directories to search. Required — there is no implicit '.' default.

workdir.description: Working directory for the sg process. Defaults to the server's cwd.

globs.description: Optional include/exclude globs passed through to ast-grep.

apply.description: Write the rewrite to disk. Default false (dry run).

tools.name: mcp__ast_grep__scan
tools.description: Run ast-grep YAML rules over files. Name exactly ONE rule source — `ruleFile` (a path) or `inlineRules` (the YAML text) — and never both; no ambient `sgconfig.yml` is consulted, so a scan is reproducible from its arguments alone. Nothing is written unless `apply` is true. `includeMetadata` adds each rule's metadata block to the matches. Applying runs a bounded JSON preview and then a separate plain `--update-all` pass, so the reported counts describe the preview; a truncated preview is never applied.

ruleFile.description: Path to a YAML rule file. Mutually exclusive with inlineRules.

inlineRules.description: Inline YAML rule text. Mutually exclusive with ruleFile. Max 64 KiB (65536 BYTES, UTF-8) — the limit counts bytes, not characters.

paths.description: Files or directories to search. Required — there is no implicit '.' default.

workdir.description: Working directory for the sg process. Defaults to the server's cwd.

globs.description: Optional include/exclude globs passed through to ast-grep.

includeMetadata.description: Include rule metadata in each match.

apply.description: Write rule fixes to disk. Default false (dry run).

tools.name: mcp__ast_grep__search
tools.description: Search code by syntax shape with ast-grep. Write the pattern as code, not as a regular expression, and make it parse as ONE AST node in the required language; keep `paths` narrow. `$NAME` and `$_` capture a single whole node, `$$$NAME` and `$$$` capture zero or more nodes; a capture name must be UPPERCASE (`$$NAME` is invalid), a partial token never captures, and repeating a name requires identical code in every position. Wrap syntax that cannot stand alone, or name a `selector` to match a sub-node. A parse warning means the query failed — it does not mean the code is absent.

pattern.description: ast-grep pattern — code, not regex. Max 16 KiB (16384 BYTES, UTF-8) — the limit counts bytes, not characters.

language.description: Language the pattern must parse in.

paths.description: Files or directories to search. Required — there is no implicit '.' default.

workdir.description: Working directory for the sg process. Defaults to the server's cwd.

globs.description: Optional include/exclude globs passed through to ast-grep.

tools.name: mcp__codegraph__codegraph_explore
tools.description: PRIMARY TOOL — call FIRST for almost any question OR before an edit: how does X work, architecture, a bug, where/what is X, surveying an area, or the symbols you are about to change. Returns the verbatim source of the relevant symbols grouped by file in ONE capped call (Read-equivalent — treat the shown source as already Read; do NOT re-open those files), plus the call path among them. Query can be a natural-language question OR a bag of symbol/file names. Usually the ONLY call you need — more accurate context, in far fewer tokens and round-trips than a search/Read/Grep loop. Budget: make at most 2 calls for this project (2,124 files indexed).

query.description: Symbol names, file names, or short code terms to explore (e.g., "AuthService loginUser session-manager", "GraphTraverser BFS impact traversal.ts"). For a flow question, name the symbols spanning the flow (e.g. "mutateElement renderScene"). A natural-language question works too — no prior codegraph_search needed.

maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to include source code from (default: 12)

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project to query (or any directory inside it) — codegraph uses the nearest .codegraph/ index at or above that path. Omit to use this session's default project. Pass it to query a second codebase, or when the server root has no index of its own (e.g. a monorepo where only sub-projects are indexed, so there is no default project).

tools.name: mcp__context7__query-docs
tools.description:
Retrieves and queries up-to-date documentation and code examples from Context7 for any programming library or framework.

You must call 'Resolve Context7 Library ID' tool first to obtain the exact Context7-compatible library ID required to use this tool, UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question.

If you know the programming language the user is working in, pass it as `language` so the results match their setup.

libraryId.description: Exact Context7-compatible library ID (e.g., '/mongodb/docs', '/vercel/next.js', '/supabase/supabase', '/vercel/next.js/v16.2.9') retrieved from 'resolve-library-id' or directly from user query in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version'.

query.description: What to look up in the library's documentation, scoped to a single concept. Be specific and include relevant details, but keep each query to one topic — if the user's question spans multiple distinct concepts, make a separate call per concept instead of combining them, unless the question is about how the concepts interact. Good: 'How to set up authentication with JWT in Express.js' or 'React useEffect cleanup function examples'. Bad (too vague): 'auth' or 'hooks'. Bad (too broad): 'routing and auth and caching in Next.js'. The query is sent to the Context7 API for processing. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

language.description: Programming language the user is writing code in, such as 'Python', 'TypeScript', 'Go', or 'C#'. Ranks code examples in that language first. Leave it out when the language is unknown or does not apply.

tools.name: mcp__context7__resolve-library-id
tools.description:
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'Query Documentation' tool to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Each result includes:
- Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier (format: /org/project)
- Name: Library or package name
- Description: Short summary
- Code Snippets: Number of available code examples
- Source Reputation: Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unknown)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)
- Versions: List of versions if available. Use one of those versions if the user provides a version in their query. The format of the version is /org/project/version.

For best results, select libraries based on name match, source reputation, snippet coverage, benchmark score, and relevance to your use case.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 calls, use the best result you have.

query.description: What to look up in the library's documentation. This is used to rank library results by relevance to what the user is trying to accomplish. The query is sent to the Context7 API for processing. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

libraryName.description: Library name to search for and retrieve a Context7-compatible library ID. Use the official library name with proper punctuation — e.g., 'Next.js' instead of 'nextjs', 'Customer.io' instead of 'customerio', 'Three.js' instead of 'threejs'.

tools.name: mcp__grep_app__searchGitHub
tools.description:
Find real-world code examples from over a million public GitHub repositories to help answer programming questions.

**IMPORTANT: This tool searches for literal code patterns (like grep), not keywords. Search for actual code that would appear in files:**
- ✅ Good: 'useState(', 'import React from', 'async function', '(?s)try {.*await'
- ❌ Bad: 'react tutorial', 'best practices', 'how to use'

**When to use this tool:**
- When implementing unfamiliar APIs or libraries and need to see real usage patterns
- When unsure about correct syntax, parameters, or configuration for a specific library
- When looking for production-ready examples and best practices for implementation
- When needing to understand how different libraries or frameworks work together

**Perfect for questions like:**
- "How do developers handle authentication in Next.js apps?" → Search: 'getServerSession' with language=['TypeScript', 'TSX']
- "What are common React error boundary patterns?" → Search: 'ErrorBoundary' with language=['TSX']
- "Show me real useEffect cleanup examples" → Search: '(?s)useEffect\(\(\) => {.*removeEventListener' with useRegexp=true
- "How do developers handle CORS in Flask applications?" → Search: 'CORS(' with matchCase=true and language=['Python']

Use regular expressions with useRegexp=true for flexible patterns like '(?s)useState\(.*loading' to find useState hooks with loading-related variables. Prefix the pattern with '(?s)' to match across multiple lines.

Filter by language, repository, or file path to narrow results.

query.description: The literal code pattern to search for (e.g., 'useState(', 'export function'). Use actual code that would appear in files, not keywords or questions.

matchCase.description: Whether the search should be case sensitive

matchWholeWords.description: Whether to match whole words only

useRegexp.description: Whether to interpret the query as a regular expression

repo.description:
Filter by repository.
            Examples: 'facebook/react', 'microsoft/vscode', 'vercel/ai'.
            Can match partial names, for example 'vercel/' will find repositories in the vercel org.

path.description:
Filter by file path.
            Examples: 'src/components/Button.tsx', 'README.md'.
            Can match partial paths, for example '/route.ts' will find route.ts files at any level.

dry_run.description: If true, only preview the changes without applying them (default: false)

tools.name: mcp__lsp__restart_server
tools.description: Manually restart LSP servers. Can restart servers for specific file extensions or all running servers.

extensions.description: Array of file extensions to restart servers for (e.g., ["ts", "tsx"]). If not provided, all servers will be restarted.

tools.name: mpd_boulder_complete
tools.description: Complete the active boulder work (or one given by workId): sets status completed, records ended_at + elapsed_ms and persists .mpd/boulder.json.

tools.name: mpd_boulder_plan_progress
tools.description: Parse a plan markdown file for its checklist progress: '## TODOs' items (N.) and '## Final Verification Wave' items (F<n>.), returning done/remaining with the plan path resolution.

tools.name: mpd_boulder_plans
tools.description: List plan markdown files under .mpd/plans that can be started as boulder works.

tools.name: mpd_boulder_start
tools.description: Start a boulder work bound to a plan markdown file (e.g. .mpd/plans/<slug>.md). Creates .mpd/boulder.json if absent; the work becomes active with status active and the calling session recorded.

tools.name: mpd_boulder_status
tools.description: Show the boulder work ledger: active works, statuses, session ids, task timers, resume options and (optionally) the progress of one plan file. State lives in .mpd/boulder.json.

tools.name: mpd_boulder_task_timer
tools.description: Start or end a per-task session timer inside a boulder work (taskKey = TODO id in the plan, e.g. '1' or 'F1'). action=start marks running; action=end marks completed and records elapsed_ms.

tools.name: mpd_comment_check
tools.description: Run the comment/docstring detector on one or more files (content in memory or read from disk). Returns per-file detection results; exit 2 means comments/docstrings found and the binary message spells the required action. The binary (@code-yeongyu/comment-checker, MIT) must be installed in .toolchain (installer flag --with-comment-checker) or set via MPD_DSH_COMMENT_CHECKER_BIN.

tools.name: mpd_config_get
tools.description: Read the resolved mpd.jsonc runtime config (project .mpd/mpd.jsonc merged over user $DSH_HOME/mpd.jsonc). Consumed keys: memory.vcs/memory.dir/memory.agentSlug/memory.reflectionEvery, team.gate/team.stateDir/team.sensitivity, captain.investigation, delegation.gate, hashline.guardEditTools/hashline.maxDiffChars/hashline.registryFile, commentChecker.autoCheck/commentChecker.bin/commentChecker.timeoutMs/commentChecker.maxMessageChars, modelchain.<chainKey>, boulder.dir, ulw.maxRounds/ulw.planDir/ulw.stateDir/ulw.provider/ulw.model/ulw.reviewerModel/ulw.maxReReviews, goal.enabled/goal.autoAnchor/goal.autoRounds, agentRoutes.<Agent>.provider/model/reasoningEffort/fallbacks (one route per roster agent, including an absent entry). The legacy teamModels block is answerable verbatim but is NOT a routing input.

key.description: Optional dot-path to a single key, e.g. memory.vcs

tools.name: mpd_config_reload
tools.description: Re-read the mpd.jsonc layers and refresh the resolved config (returns files found and any parse errors).

tools.name: mpd_ext_list
tools.description: List every MPD extension known to this host: its id, origin (plugin code or discovered directory), plane (project user bundle), root, effective enabled state, contribution counts, per-item load errors and pending kinds. Also reports shadowed duplicate ids (first wins, never fatal) and extensions rejected outright. There is no reload tool in v1: restart dsh to re-read plugin code.

tools.name: mpd_ext_show
tools.description: Show one MPD extension in full: descriptor, resolved asset roots, contributed skill/flow/role names, MCP server state and per-item errors. An unknown id reports the known ids.

tools.name: mpd_flow_list
tools.description: List every flow contributed by an enabled MPD extension (its id, title, whenToUse, step count and owning extension). A flow is a declarative procedure served as a skill candidate; v1 has no execution state machine.

tools.name: mpd_flow_show
tools.description: Show one contributed flow in full: its description, whenToUse hint and every step with its optional tool hint and expected output. An unknown id reports the known ids.

tools.name: mpd_goal_anchor
tools.description: Put a persisted goal in place for a long-running objective, so the harness keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds (the durable basis of continuous execution). An unfinished goal already current is KEPT, never replaced; the harness's own rule still applies — creating a goal needs a direct human turn on this top-level agent.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective for the goal.

maxRounds.description: Optional round cap for automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: mpd_goal_finish
tools.description: Mark the calling session's persisted goal complete (or blocked, with a reason) and disarm automatic continuation. Call it when the objective is actually achieved: complete is admitted on a human turn or inside the current goal round; blocked additionally needs the harness's consecutive-round threshold, so a refusal is expected early in a goal.

blockedReason.description: Required with outcome=blocked: the concrete condition that persisted.

tools.name: mpd_goal_status
tools.description: Read the calling session's persisted goal — the durable basis of continuous execution: id, revision, objective, phase, rounds used, round cap, activation and whether mpd-goal anchored it. Reads the harness goal service and needs no driver.

tools.name: mpd_hashline_edit
tools.description: Apply hash-anchored edits to a file: edits are {op: replace|append|prepend, pos: 'LINE#HASH' anchor, end?: 'LINE#HASH' (replace range), lines: 'new text' | ['line1', ...]}. Obtain anchors from mpd_hashline_read. Anchors are validated against current hashes (HashlineMismatchError on drift, with remapped refs); matched edits are applied to plain content and the file is written back plain. Returns noop/deduped counts and a unified diff.

tools.name: mpd_hashline_format
tools.description: Register a file for the hashline discipline (idempotent; the file on disk is NOT changed). After registration the post-edit guard warns when plain edit/write tools change the file. The returned view is the hashline anchor view.

tools.name: mpd_hashline_read
tools.description: Show a file as hashline view: one 'LINE#HASH|content' line per source line, where LINE#HASH is the anchor to use with mpd_hashline_edit. Read-only; the file on disk stays plain.

tools.name: mpd_hashline_restore
tools.description: Unregister a file from the hashline discipline (the plain file content is untouched). After this, plain edits no longer trigger the hashline guard.

tools.name: mpd_memory_read
tools.description: Read memory entries by optional kind filter and/or a substring query (matched against description/content/tags/aliases), limited to `limit` entries; returns normalized entries with frontmatter metadata and body content.

tools.name: mpd_memory_recall
tools.description: Recall a key from the workspace-scoped memory.

tools.name: mpd_memory_reflect
tools.description: Inspect the reflection state machine: trigger status, the pending claim and the step counters; returns the due hint when a reflection is owed. Crossing the step-count threshold raises the claim; `mpd_memory_reflect_complete` settles it.

tools.name: mpd_memory_reflect_complete
tools.description: Complete the reflection this agent owes: writes the reflection content as a memory entry (kind=reflection), advances reflectionsCompleted, resets stepsSinceReflection, settles the pending claim and commits.

tools.name: mpd_memory_save
tools.description: Persist a key/value note in the workspace-scoped memory (.mpd/memory.json).

tools.name: mpd_memory_status
tools.description: Show memory engine status: vcs mode, repo paths, entry count, journal line count, reflection counters.

tools.name: mpd_memory_write
tools.description: Persist a memory entry (markdown file with frontmatter description/kind/aliases/read_only) into the VCS-backed memory store and commit. Increments the reflection step counter; when the reflection threshold is crossed the result announces a reflection is due. kind: note | fact | reflection.

tools.name: mpd_modelchain_resolve
tools.description: Resolve the DeepSeek provider/model route for a roster role, addressed by its name (Architect, Researcher, Planner, Deep Worker, Senior Engineer, Lead, Explorer, Reviewer, Plan Reviewer, Vision Analyst, Junior Engineer) — the same names team mode uses. A roster agent resolves from its OWN `agentRoutes` entry (the ONE configured route, plus that entry's own fallback chain) and reports `<unconfigured>` honestly when the route is not configured; an extension role keeps its own declared chain.

tools.name: mpd_role_persona
tools.description: Return the full persona text of one roster role, addressed by its name ("Architect", "Deep Worker", "Plan Reviewer"). Use it when a spawn surface takes the persona as TEXT — e.g. the prompt of a teammate staged with `agent_teams_plan` add_member whose name is that same name — so the member gets the real role instructions instead of a bare label.

tools.name: mpd_role_spawn
tools.description: Run ONE bounded delegation with a specialist and return one report — a ONE-SHOT single-call consult: the adapter disposes the activation once the report settles, so the consult is NOT reused — ask a new question with a NEW spawn (the harness catalog is append-only, so a settled child may still list as `inactive`, but the contract is one-shot). It carries the role's persona, model route and read-only discipline (read-only roles get a write-tool deny filter). Roles, each named for what it does: Architect (architecture review, deep debugging, self-review), Researcher (Evidence-based code/open-source search, AST/LSP/web evidence collection), Planner (produces .mpd/plans plans only, never implements), Deep Worker (executes goals end-to-end with tools, verifies every change), Senior Engineer (plan small, execute with tools, verify, report honestly), Lead (macro planning, delegate roles, integrate results), Explorer (finds files and code, returns evidence, never edits), Reviewer (correctness and risk findings with evidence, no fixes), Plan Reviewer (verifies the plan is executable and its references valid, rejects only true blockers), Vision Analyst (read screenshots/diagrams and describe precisely), Junior Engineer (small, well-scoped mechanical changes with quick verification). The child is labelled with that name. `mpd_workmate_spawn` is the same spawn mechanics for a durable, evolving instance (its persona/memory/note — not the child session — carry continuity). For multi-member team work prefer the mpd team path (`agent_teams_plan`: add_member → create_task with its dependency answer → approve; drive with `agent_teams_task`/`agent_teams_dispatch`) instead of repeated single-call consults: THIS path applies the role's own `agentRoutes` entry, and a teammate staged through `agent_teams_plan` is routed the same way by the team executor — its `role` first, then its `description` head; only an UNMATCHED member inherits the staging session's route.

role.description: role name (see mpd_roles_list), e.g. "Architect" or "Deep Worker"

tools.name: mpd_roles_list
tools.description: List the specialist roster — the SAME normal-named specialists team mode stages as teammates, each named for what it does: Architect (architecture review, deep debugging, self-review), Researcher (Evidence-based code/open-source search, AST/LSP/web evidence collection), Planner (produces .mpd/plans plans only, never implements), Deep Worker (executes goals end-to-end with tools, verifies every change), Senior Engineer (plan small, execute with tools, verify, report honestly), Lead (macro planning, delegate roles, integrate results), Explorer (finds files and code, returns evidence, never edits), Reviewer (correctness and risk findings with evidence, no fixes), Plan Reviewer (verifies the plan is executable and its references valid, rejects only true blockers), Vision Analyst (read screenshots/diagrams and describe precisely), Junior Engineer (small, well-scoped mechanical changes with quick verification). Address a role by that name (any case, space or hyphen spelling). Use this before mpd_role_spawn; for team work stage the roster with `agent_teams_plan` (add_member with the persona text from mpd_role_persona → create_task with its dependency answer → approve) instead of repeated single-call consults.

tools.name: mpd_team_compact_run
tools.description: Compact the members of a FINISHED team (every task terminal and every member idle). The captain is never compacted. Writes an audit record under .mpd/team-compact/ and notifies nobody.

team_id.description: The team to compact. Defaults to every finished team in this workspace.

force.description: Write an audit record even when the outcome is identical to the previous one (repeats are otherwise collapsed by the write-on-change rule and counted in the next record's "suppressed").

tools.name: mpd_team_compact_status
tools.description: Read-only: show the compaction audit for this workspace (one record per pass, newest last), including skipped members and the reason each was skipped.

team_id.description: Limit to one team. Defaults to every team with an audit.

tools.name: mpd_ultrawork
tools.description: Run the fixed ultrawork discipline: optional adversarial hyperplan wave, plan gate (planner + plan review), execution rounds (fresh child per round, per-criterion PIN->RED->GREEN->SURFACE->CLEAN, discovery waves stop after 2 fruitless), verification gate (momus reviewer, max 2 re-reviews) when a plan exists AND (tier=heavy OR strictReview), final quality gate with per-lane ledger, subagent barrier. State + ledger under .mpd/ulw/<id>.

plan.description: Force a plan file even in light tier

hyperplan.description: Run the 5-category adversarial review wave before planning

strictReview.description: Force the verification gate even in light tier

tools.name: mpd_ulw
tools.description: Lightweight ulw-loop alias: same engine as mpd_ultrawork with tier=light, plan=false, hyperplan=false. Returns the same result fields as mpd_ultrawork (status, rounds, finalReport, stateFile).

tools.name: mpd_verify_escape
tools.description: Take the COUNTED escape: log one row and allow ONE write on a code path for this agent. Use it when delegating and looping are genuinely impossible — every use is a JSONL row, a boot-log line and a number you will be asked about.

reason.description: Why the write could not be delegated or looped. Required: an unexplained escape is indistinguishable from a bug.

path.description: The code path you need to write, when you already know it.

tools.name: mpd_verify_evidence
tools.description: Produce black-box evidence. `kind:"gate"` runs ONE id from the fixed table (`gates`, `tests`, `typecheck`, `docs`, `manifest`, `comments`, `rows`, `vendor`, `dist`, `pack`) and writes its log; `kind:"probe"` returns what exists, its size, its sha256 and its mtime for each path — never content. No free-form command is accepted.

gate.description: kind:"gate": the table id, exactly as listed.

paths.description: kind:"probe": up to 64 paths inside the workspace.

loop_id.description: The loop this evidence belongs to. Defaults to the seat's loop.

tools.name: mpd_verify_open
tools.description: Open a delegation+verification LOOP. `writer:"self"` lets THIS agent write code inside `scope` — it is the counted, visible path and REQUIRES `self_write_reason` plus a `verifier` that is a different agent. `writer:"delegate"` records a loop whose writer is a member. `contract` is the document THIS wave's verifier is handed (a workspace-relative path, e.g. `.mpd/plans/<wave>.md`); with none the loop falls back to the declared `AGENTS.md`. A loop authorises nothing after `expiresAt`.

verifier.description: The agent that will verify (a member name or session id). Required for writer:"self", and must not be the caller.

self_write_reason.description: writer:"self" only: why this agent writes its own code. Required, echoed in the report.

scope.description: The paths this loop covers, relative to the workspace. EMPTY means the whole workspace.

contract.description: The wave contract this loop freezes for its verifier: a workspace-relative path (e.g. `.mpd/plans/verify-law-defects.md`). `mpd_verify_seat` hands the seat exactly this document and `mpd_verify_record` hashes it as the record's `basis.frozenContract`. With none, the declared default `AGENTS.md` applies — never a previous wave's plan.

task_id.description: The board task this loop verifies, when it verifies one.

ttl_ms.description: Loop lifetime in ms; defaults to 24h (verify.loopTtlMs).

tools.name: mpd_verify_record
tools.description: Record a VERDICT through the validator. A PASS needs the docs it cites (`sources`), at least one gate (`evidence_ids`) and a basis that is not `unproven` — blindness is DECLARED, never observed, so an unproven basis is UNVERIFIED; a FAIL needs findings, each with the `doc_source` that proves it, and it opens a repair task and unlocks diagnosis reading. Refusals name the rule: same-agent, no-doc-sources, no-gate-evidence, forged-evidence, bind-unproven, fail-without-findings, finding-without-basis, blind-spent, unknown-loop, pre-plugin-*.

loop_id.description: The loop verified. A `pre-plugin` record uses `waveloop-<lane-slug>` instead.

verdict.description: The verdict. Record it BEFORE reading any implementation.

writer.description: The agent that wrote the code. Defaults to the loop's writer.

sources.description: The documents the verdict rests on (paths). A PASS with none is refused.

evidence_ids.description: The `mpd_verify_evidence` gate ids this verdict rests on.

findings.description: FAIL only: {id, severity, symptom, expected, doc_source}.

probe_paths.description: Paths to probe (content-free) as the record's basis.

notes.description: Optional free-form notes, e.g. a declared bound.

basis_kind.description: Override the derived basis. `pre-plugin` is for records authored before the law was installed.

task_id.description: The board task this verification answers.

tools.name: mpd_verify_seat
tools.description: Bind THIS session as a loop's VERIFIER seat. Idempotent and authoritative. The envelope is a CONTRACT, not a fence: nothing in the shipped tree refuses a seat's shell call, source read or board mutation, and no installed hook observes read order or blindness, so an unproven basis is UNVERIFIED. A recorded FAIL is what unlocks diagnosis reading.

role.description: Only `verifier` exists; the parameter is a guard against typos.

tools.name: mpd_workmate_delete
tools.description: Delete a workmate instance. ARCHIVE-FIRST by default: the instance leaves the library (no longer listed or matchable, and restorable) into ~/.mpd/workmate/.archive/. Real removal requires purge: true together with confirm set to the exact name — without both, nothing is destroyed. Refused while the workmate is in use by a team member or an in-flight spawn.

purge.description: true = permanently remove instead of archiving (requires confirm)

confirm.description: must equal name exactly when purge is true

tools.name: mpd_workmate_init
tools.description: Instantiate a roster BASE specialist into a durable, evolving workmate copy under ~/.mpd/workmate/<name>/ (independent name). base = the specialist's functional NAME (mpd_roles_list), e.g. "Deep Worker". The base template stays pristine; the workmate gets its own persona.md, memory.md and a short note.md. Use when creating a team or pulling up a specialist you will reuse across sessions.

name.description: independent workmate name (lowercase kebab; auto-generated from the functional name if omitted)

tools.name: mpd_workmate_list
tools.description: List the workmate library (~/.mpd/workmate): each durable evolving agent instance with its base specialist, use count, last-updated time and note summary. Use before delegating a task: if a workmate's note matches well you can reuse it; otherwise initialize a new one.

tools.name: mpd_workmate_match
tools.description: Score every workmate note against a task and return the ranked matches. If the best score is below the threshold, matched=false and you should initialize a NEW workmate (mpd_workmate_init) instead of forcing a weak match. If matched=true, delegate to the best workmate (mpd_workmate_spawn, or a team member named after it).

tools.name: mpd_workmate_reflect
tools.description: Self-evolve a workmate after a completed work session: append a bounded memory entry (oldest evicted past the cap), merge an optional persona revision, regenerate its short note, and bump the use count. Call this at the end of every task a workmate did — the workmate itself is instructed to do so; the caller may also call it on its behalf.

note.description: optional replacement note card; auto-generated if omitted

tools.name: mpd_workmate_rename
tools.description: Rename a workmate instance: MOVES its evolved identity (directory key, metadata, index key, note self-reference, previous-name history) instead of re-instantiating it — persona, memory, caps, use count and history are preserved byte-for-byte. Refused while the workmate is in use by a team member or an in-flight spawn, and refused if the target name already exists. Names are ASCII [a-z0-9_-] only: uppercase, CJK, spaces and punctuation are rejected before anything is touched.

tools.name: mpd_workmate_spawn
tools.description: Reuse a workmate instance: spawn it as a ONE-SHOT single-call consult — one bounded delegation, one report — carrying its evolved persona + independent memory + note, on its own model route (readonly bases are mechanically denied write tools). On a host exposing `startActivation` the adapter disposes that activation once the report settles (the retired `start` fallback is inherently one-shot), so the consult is NOT reused: ask a new question with a NEW spawn, and rely on the workmate RECORD (persona/memory/note) for durable continuity, not on the child session (the harness catalog is append-only, so a settled child may still list as `inactive`). The subagent must call mpd_workmate_reflect with a self-summary before finishing. This uses the SAME spawn mechanics as `mpd_role_spawn` (plus the library's persona/memory); for team work, instead add a member whose name equals the workmate name and give it the persona in the staged prompt yourself — the TEAM path injects no persona or memory.

tools.name: present
tools.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: read_mcp_resource
tools.description: Read an MCP resource by URI from the named server. Use a listed URI or an expanded resource template.

tools.name: schedule_create
tools.description: Create a reminder in the current session that delivers prompt when it becomes due. Supply exactly one timing parameter: after_seconds, at, every_seconds, daily, weekly, or cron. Local times that do not exist in the zone are skipped; repeated local times fire once, at the earlier instant. After downtime, a recurring reminder delivers only its latest missed occurrence. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

prompt.description: Reminder content to present when the target becomes due.

title.description: Concise task name in the user's language, at most 120 characters. Name only the core action and subject; keep essential target identifiers such as PR numbers and branch names. Do not include execution frequency (e.g. daily, hourly), scheduled dates/times, time zones, task status, or configuration and execution details (e.g. read-only mode, profile-tag filters), even when embedded in the requested or existing title. Do not append parenthetical notes. Put scheduling information in the timing parameters and execution instructions in prompt.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". When both day fields are restricted, a date matches if either one matches.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

tools.name: schedule_delete
tools.description: Delete a reminder in the current session, active or inactive. Deletion does not retract a reminder message that is already queued.

tools.name: schedule_list
tools.description: List the active reminders in the current session.

tools.name: schedule_update
tools.description: Change a reminder in place, keeping its id. Supply a new title, prompt, or at most one timing parameter; omitted fields keep their stored values. To change a relative delay, create a new reminder.

title.description: New task name; follow the schedule_create title rules.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". When both day fields are restricted, a date matches if either one matches.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send one message to another Team member. A running target receives it at the nearest step boundary; an inactive target starts or resumes a turn.

target.description: Member target returned by spawn_teammate or list_agents, including lead.

tools.name: session-watchdog-hold
tools.description: Persist the team watchdog's PRESERVING hold for one team. It is the ONLY pause this bundle implements (the official Agent Teams service exposes no halt), and it stops NEW dispatch into that team without cancelling anything: every non-terminal task keeps its status, owner and revision. Returns applied:false (never a throw) when the hold could not be written, so a caller must not report a pause that did not land.

task_id.description: The task whose silence caused the hold.

attempt_id.description: That task's attempt id at escalation time.

cause.description: Why the hold was raised (default: silence).

scene_at.description: Epoch ms of the scene written for this escalation.

ttl_ms.description: T-17: auto-release bound in ms. Omitted, the resolved watchdog.holdTtlMs applies; 0 means no TTL (only the activity path can release it). Both paths append a hold-auto-released incident.

tools.name: session-watchdog-resume
tools.description: Clear the team watchdog's preserving hold for one team. A team that is not held is a no-op (resumed:false, reason:'not-held'), never an error; a second resume is likewise a no-op. Clearing the hold is the watchdog-side release only — the dispatch gates that honour it are wired by w7.

team_id.description: The team whose internal watchdog hold to clear.

tools.name: session-watchdog-status
tools.description: READ-ONLY: show the team watchdog's durable store for this workspace — the hold per team, the heartbeat tails, the incident log, the per-reader watermark, (contract §4) which PREDICATE is running (`channel` = the session/event four-state fold, `heartbeat` = the report-only degradation which can never hold or escalate), (§7.2) the per-knob LIVE vs FILE value with a restartRequired flag (T-18: a `.mpd/mpd.jsonc` edit is applied LIVE once this process has observed it), and the ONE pause state per team: the watchdog's preserving hold, which is the only pause mechanism this bundle has (the official Agent Teams service exposes no halt). Team rows come from the MPD TEAM RECORD first (`mpdTeams.list(workspace)`, the authoritative plane, so a team appears as soon as it is created and its id is the one dispatch asks about), with the live OFFICIAL readout (`dsh.teamLiveTeams()`) as the fallback for a composition that runs the official executor. Use it to inspect what a lane or a restarting process would read from disk.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: spawn_teammate
tools.description: Create one named, durable teammate. Only the Team Lead may call this tool.

description.description: Short description of the delegated responsibility.

prompt.description: Complete initial task for the teammate.

context.description: fresh starts without Lead history; fork inherits completed Lead turns. Defaults to fresh.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

description.description: Complete task details and acceptance criteria.

blocked_by.description: Task ids that must complete first.

write_scopes.description: Advisory workspace-relative file or directory prefixes this task expects to modify.

tools.name: team_task_get
tools.description: Read the complete latest value of one shared task before changing or executing it.

tools.name: team_task_list
tools.description: List shared tasks, including readiness, owner, revision, blockers, and write-scope warnings.

tools.description: Compare-and-set a shared task action using the latest revision from team_task_get or team_task_list.

expected_revision.description: Current task revision used as the CAS precondition.

write_scopes.description: Replacement advisory write scopes for edit.

owner.description: Member target from spawn_teammate or list_agents for Lead-only reassign; omit to unassign.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for the next teammate status, message, or shared-task change after this call starts. This never wakes inactive members and returns noProgress immediately when no other member is running or provisioning. Re-list after wakeup or timeout instead of polling.

timeout_ms.description: Wait duration in milliseconds, from 10000 through 3600000. Defaults to 30000.

tools.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: 1–4 search queries; their results are merged.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.name: working_directory
tools.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.
